properties.projname: Belmont Heights Gravity Sewer CIPP Lining
properties.projdesc: This project includes the rehabilitation of approximately 143,264 linear feet of 8-inch, 5,581 linear feet of 10-inch, 1,604 linear feet of 12-inch, 3,317 linear feet of 15-inch, and 3,744 linear feet of 18-inch diameter gravity sewers and the rehabilitation of manholes.
properties.rationale: The collection system rehabilitation project will restore aging sewer pipes and manholes to restore their service life.  Project impacts will be minimal compared to a collection system “open cut” replacement project since the rehabilitation methods are trenchless.  The collection system rehabilitation will reduce pipeline failures and blockages that cause wastewater overflows that impact public health, safety, and the environment.  Additional project benefits include reduction in leaks that allow ground water and stormwater runoff to enter the collection system and cause wastewater overflows, reduction in energy needed to treat and convey the additional wastewater flow caused by leaking pipelines/manholes and reduction in pipeline failures that cause roadway depressions and cave ins.

properties.projdesc: This project provides for the rehabilitation of the force main that serves the Sulphur Springs Pumping Station located at 7902 N 13th St. The scope includes approximately 24,500 linear feet of 42” and 48” force main extending to the force main discharge at E 29th Ave and N 26th St. As Part of this project the existing force main will be cleaned and rehabilitated to address significant clogging. The cleaning process will allow for a detailed inspection to assess overall condition of the force main. To maintain continuous service during cleaning, an abandoned force main in the vicinity will be reactivated and temporarily placed in service as a bypass to ensure the normal high flows from the PS are conveyed without interruption. The old force main will be left available long after the project is complete, providing more flexibility and resiliency for future challenges.
properties.rationale: The force main rehabilitation project will restore critical wastewater infrastructure by removing buildup and blockages that restrict flow and increase the risk of system failure. Cleaning the pipeline will improve the reliability and help prevent wastewater overflows that could impact the public health and environment, as well as enhance the overall system performance and extend service life of existing infrastructure.

properties.projdesc: This project provides for the rehabilitation of the force main that serves the Ybor Pumping Station located at 1302 N 25th St. The scope includes approximately 1,090 feet of 72” force main along 26th Street, which will be rehabilitated or replaced due to its deteriorated condition. As a part of this project, a new 36” force main will be constructed from the Ybor Station to the intersection of 34th street and 3rd avenue to function as a temporary bypass to divert the normal high flows from the Ybor Pump Station during the replacement of the existing 72”. The 36” FM will be left available long after the project is complete, providing more flexibility and resiliency for future challenges.
properties.rationale: The force main replacement project will replace aging, deteriorated pipelines that have reached the end of their useful life and are susceptible to failure that can cause wastewater overflows that impact public health, safety, and the environment. The new force main will provide additional capacity for future development and lower energy costs of public and private pumping stations. The addition of the new force main provides added operational flexibility and resiliency to better serve the community during future maintenance activities and high flow conditions.
